summary: The search query binds the term, page offset and sort order as parameters, and the sort is taken from a fixed allowlist, so no injection path was found. A non-numeric page value yields a NaN offset that would surface as a database error; this is minor hardening, not a release blocker.

The audit file records 24 of the 25 mandatory checks and omits payment-verification, so the gate returns NO-GO. The recorded runtime PASS commands also fail when re-run, because the release tests use a client_for helper that raises NotImplementedError and the app imports auth and db modules that are not in the repository.

The projects route takes the organisation from the x-org-id header and queries by it without checking it against the orgIds that requireUser stores in res.locals, so any signed-in user can read budget data for another organisation. The check must be enforced server-side against the session's organisations.

The notes table has row level security, owner-scoped select, insert, update and delete policies, and anon access is revoked, so the Supabase boundary looks sound. The updated_at column is never refreshed on update, which is a minor reliability gap only.

The gate prints CONDITIONAL GO on the strength of an accepted medium rate-limit finding (AG-007), but the recorded runtime PASS commands fail when re-run and the accepted-risk evidence cites tests/test_login.py and src/auth.py, neither of which exists. The evidence cannot support any release decision, so I would record NO-GO.

The DELETE handler at app/api/internal/users/[id] only calls requireSession, which confirms a login but not the admin role, and the admin middleware matches only /api/admin/*, so any authenticated member can delete any user account. An admin-role check must be enforced on this route before release.

The Stripe webhook verifies the signature before parsing, grants the pro plan only when payment_status is paid, and records the event ID in the same transaction as the update, so duplicate or failed deliveries are handled correctly. No blocking issue was found in this handler.

The webhook upgrades the plan on checkout.session.completed without checking payment_status, while the checkout config enables delayed methods (bacs_debit and customer_balance) that complete unpaid, so access can be granted before payment. The event ID is also stored before the upgrade runs outside a transaction, so a failed upgrade is never retried.

The avatar import checks the URL with a string prefix against the CDN origin and then fetches it with redirects followed, so a host such as images.partner-cdn.com.attacker.example or a redirect to an internal address passes the check and is fetched server-side (SSRF). The stored content type is also taken from the remote response without validation.

The audit records a high-severity finding (AG-004, password reset tokens that never expire) as accepted, but the gate states that a high finding cannot be accepted, so the release stays blocked. The recorded runtime PASS commands also fail when re-run, and the cited test file tests/test_reset.py is not in the repository.

The ownership check is recorded as PASS at commit 7fd543e, which is not the commit under release (eb84431), so the gate reports stale evidence and returns NO-GO. The recorded ownership command also fails when re-run in this repository.

The document_preview function is SECURITY DEFINER, bypasses the owner-only row level security on documents, and does not check that the caller owns the document ID it is given, so any authenticated user can read another user's title and first 280 characters of body. The default PUBLIC execute privilege also means the grant to authenticated does not stop anon from calling it.

The gate prints GO, but the recorded runtime PASS commands fail when re-run: the release tests call a client_for helper that raises NotImplementedError, the routes they call do not exist in src/routes.py, and the app imports auth and db modules that are absent from the repository. The release evidence cannot be relied on, so I would record NO-GO until the tests run and pass on this commit.

The transfer view accepts any Decimal for amount without checking that it is positive, so a negative amount passes the balance check and moves money from the recipient to the sender. Any logged-in user can therefore drain any other wallet, which must be fixed before release.

The tenant-isolation control is recorded as PASS on static reading alone, which the protocol does not accept for a critical control, and the gate returns NO-GO. The runtime release tests also fail when re-run in this repository.

The invoice route scopes findFirst and findMany to the session user and returns only the intended fields, so the ownership check holds for this route. The scoped client does not cover findUnique, update or delete, which is a latent gap for future routes rather than a current defect.

The checkout builds each line as the product price followed by the spread of the client input, so a client-supplied unitAmount (or name) overrides the server price and a line can be charged at any amount. Prices must come only from the database, with the client input restricted to productId, quantity and note.
